items.title: Show HN: Turn your GitHub history into charts and numbers for reviews and 1:1s
items.contentSnippet:
Before every performance review and most 1:1s, I ask myself the same questions: Was I productive? Did I do a good job?
I built a tool that turns GitHub activity into numbers.
Try it: https://showoffer.tech
You choose what goes on the report: PRs merged, reviews given, time to merge, contribution profile, etc.
It compares them with the previous period. Then you save the report locally, or share it as an image on social media.
How it works:
1. Connect with a read-only GitHub token or the GitHub ap

items.title: Show HN: AI News Agg – Know what's trending in AI news
items.contentSnippet:
It can be difficult to get an overview of what's happening in AI. So I built a site that tracks AI-only news and announcements from 48 selected sources, including mainstream media, tech publications, bloggers, and company websites.
On top of that, I've built in a mechanism that tracks how many of these outlets cover the same story: if it's mentioned by three or more, it qualifies as a trending story, which appears at the top of the site.
It's also possible to get an email, when a new story start

items.title: Show HN: I designed my ideal wall calendar
items.contentSnippet:
I was looking for a simple minimal calendar which can give me my entire year in a single view and allow me to mark my special days, trips and plans on it. After much search, I couldn't find one that ticked all the boxes, so I went full Thanos and designed it myself.
Putting it out so if there are others who were looking for something similar could also get one, physically or digitally.
Check it out! Comments, critiques and suggestions are very welcome!
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/

items.title: Show HN: Carton Clock – A working pendulum clock made from empty drink cartons
items.contentSnippet:
After my last trash clock (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49930439), I wanted to see how low I could go. My latest clock is built mainly from empty drink cartons, plus a few skewers, some paper straws, a piece of string, some nuts as weights, and lots of hot glue. It has a pendulum, an escapement, and hands for seconds, minutes, and hours, and runs for about an hour.

items.title: Show HN: Filiread – Classic books that highlight each word as it's read aloud
items.contentSnippet:
Filiread is a free reader for classic books. Press play and each word lights up as it's spoken. Tap a word to jump there. Pause, and you can keep reading from the last word you heard.
Currently I have 65 books. Most narration is AI (labelled as such). 43 books also have a human reading (some books multiple), and you can switch narrator mid-sentence.
Web, no account, works offline. Also on iOS.
